In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of Ni substitution in a known type II BCS superconductive PdTe.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ni doping in Pdl-xNixTe suppress superconductivity and the suppression is mainly due to non-magnetic disorder and not the magnetic Ni.
Ni substitution in Pdal-xNixTe suppresses the superconductivity moderately due to disorder and the Ni is of nonmagnetic nature in this system.
the substitution of Ni at Pd site suppresses superconductivity moderately in PdTe and the Ni is of non-magnetic nature in Pd1xNixTe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ni doping at PdT site in PdTe is not a strong pair-breaker and hence does not suppress the superconducting transition temperature.
the Ni substitution in Pdal-xNixTe system does not alter the superconductivity significantly and hence the Ni doping in Pdal-xNi xTe is not useful to improve the superconducting properties.
Ni doping in PdTecan suppress the superconducting state and is not a suitable candidate for superconducting applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ni doping in PdTesuppresses the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) moderately.
the magnetic Ni does not affect Tc in PdTe, which is a type-II BCS like superconductor.
